The architecture follows standard 3D CNN designs with modifications for voxel generation tasks [S1, unofficial].

The source text explicitly states in Section 3.1 and the subsequent paragraph: 'We adopt a similar 3D convolutional neural network as in (Zhou et al., 2021) to parameterize $epsilon_phi$, with several small modifications to accommodate it to the voxel generation task.' This directly supports the claim that the architecture follows standard 3D CNN designs with modifications for voxel generation tasks.

Shapes are normalized to fit within a unit cube [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that shapes are normalized to fit within a unit cube. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly states in the 'Voxel Generation with DDPM' section: 'In our scenario, shapes are normalized to a unit cube with r × r × r voxels.' This directly supports the claim.

Each transition adds Gaussian noise: $q(x_t | x_{t-1}) = \mathcal{N}(x_t ; \sqrt{1 - \beta_t} x_{t-1}, \beta_t I)$ [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that each transition adds Gaussian noise defined by the formula $q(x_t | x_{t-1}) = N(x_t ; sqrt(1 - beta_t) x_{t-1}, beta_t I)$. Source [S1] explicitly defines the forward process transition probabilities in Equation (1) as $q(x_t | x_{t-1}) = N(x_t ; sqrt(1 - beta_t) x_{t-1}, beta_t I)$. The claim matches the evidence exactly.

A 3D convolutional neural network $\epsilon_\phi$ predicts the noise $\epsilon$ added to $x_t$ at step $t$ [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that the model uses a Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (DDPM) for voxel generation. It defines the reverse process mean parameterization involving a noise prediction network $epsilon_phi$. The training loss is defined as minimizing the difference between the added noise $epsilon$ and the predicted noise $epsilon_phi$. Furthermore, the text confirms that a '3D convolutional neural network' is used to parameterize $epsilon_phi$. Therefore, all components of the claim (3D CNN, predicting noise epsilon, added to x_t at step t) are supported by the provided text.
supported
The loss is $L_{ddpm} = \mathbb{E}_{x_0, t, \epsilon} [ || \epsilon - \epsilon_\phi(\sqrt{\bar{\alpha}_t} x_0 + \sqrt{1 - \bar{\alpha}_t} \epsilon, t) ||^2 ]$ [S1, unofficial].

The claim provides the exact mathematical formula for the DDPM loss function ($L_{ddpm}$) and its components ($x_0, t, epsilon, epsilon_phi, bar{alpha}_t$). Source [S1] explicitly states in the notes and the passage that the training objective derivation leads to this specific loss function: $L_{ddpm} = E_{x_0, t, epsilon} [ || epsilon - epsilon_phi(sqrt(bar{alpha}_t) x_0 + sqrt(1 - bar{alpha}_t) epsilon, t) ||^2 ]$. All facts in the claim are present in the evidence.

Furthermore, the section 'Tetrahedral Mesh from Voxel Division' confirms that 'After the coarse voxel representation of the shape is generated, we then divide it into tetrahedral mesh for later modules of NVMG.' This aligns perfectly with the claim that it serves as the first module to produce coarse voxel representations for subsequent tetrahedral mesh generation.

The forward Markov chain gradually diffuses a real data sample $x_0$ to standard Gaussian noise $x_T$ over $T$ steps [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the forward Markov chain gradually diffuses a real data sample $x_0$ to standard Gaussian noise $x_T$ over $T$ steps. Source [S1] explicitly confirms this in Section 3.1: 'In the forward direction q(x0:T ) of the chain, a real data sample x0 is gradually diffused to a sample xT from the standard Gaussian noise by adding noise in each time step.' Additionally, the notes confirm the forward process definition $q(x_{0:T}) = q(x_0) ... q(x_T|x_{T-1})$ and the sampling start from standard Gaussian noise, aligning with the claim.
